Paper [1] directly provides a probabilistic upper bound on how far the actor parameter stays from the optimal value in a two-timescale actor-critic (slow actor, fast critic) setting. It derives a uniform all-time high-probability concentration bound showing that after some finite time the actor parameter enters a “safe region” and remains within it thereafter with high probability, with an explicit bound on the actor error ||θ_k−θ*|| that holds for all k beyond a threshold.

Specifically, [1] states that with probability at least 1−µ1−µ2, the actor error is bounded by an expression that decreases with k (and depends on algorithm parameters µ1, µ2 and n0), and it reports experiments where actor error diminishes with the number of actor updates. Other provided papers discuss two-timescale actor-critic in different ways (e.g., convergence under Markovian noise [3] or second-order actor-critic under two-timescale assumptions [5]), but only [1] gives the requested probabilistic “distance-from-optimum” upper limit.
